title: Backward Alarm Clock

raw.title: Backward Alarm Clock
raw.everydayGoal: Wake up at 7 AM after setting alarm
raw.normalExpectation: Alarm rings at set time; hands move forward.
raw.impossibleRule: The clock's hands move backward whenever the alarm is set, so time appears to run in reverse; the alarm rings only when the hands return to midnight.
raw.visibleTrigger: Opa sets alarm for 7:00, the hour hand starts cranking counterclockwise.
raw.whyThisObject: Clock is meant to measure forward time; reversing hands makes scheduled wake-up impossible.
raw.goalRuleRelationship: Setting the alarm to a future time causes the clock to move backward away from that time, so the alarm will never ring at 7 AM.
raw.frameZeroDescription: Opa sits up in bed, staring at a bedside clock whose hour hand is moving backward past 6, while the alarm hand points to 7.

beats.strategy: Opa manually winds the clock forward to 6:59, expecting the alarm soon.
beats.visibleConsequence: As soon as he releases, the hands spin backward rapidly to 3:00.
beats.newInformation: Manual forward adjustment is undone by the reverse mechanism.

beats.strategy: Opa turns the alarm off and just watches the clock to see what time it shows.
beats.visibleConsequence: The hands freeze, then twitch backward one minute for every real second that passes.
beats.newInformation: Without alarm set, the clock still runs backward but slower.

beats.strategy: Opa sets the alarm for a time that already appears behind the current hand position, like 2:00, hoping it will trigger quickly.
beats.visibleConsequence: The alarm rings immediately, but the hands jump forward to noon, and the ringing reverses itself into a silent vacuum of sound.
beats.newInformation: Triggering the alarm causes time to jump forward to noon and sound to invert.

beats.strategy: Opa unplugs the clock and uses his phone to check the actual time.
beats.visibleConsequence: The clock's display reappears on his phone screen, showing the same backward time, and the phone's alarm icon turns into an hourglass.
beats.newInformation: The clock's impossible rule spreads to other time-keeping devices.

beats.strategy: Opa gives up and falls back asleep.
beats.visibleConsequence: The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM.
beats.newInformation: The backward time eventually catches up to the correct wake hour, but day and night are swapped.

raw.finalPayoff: The clock chimes twelve times in reverse, and Opa wakes up at 7 AM, but the clock reads 7 PM.
raw.suggestedPayoffFamily: delayed consequence / goal reached wrongly via causal inversion
raw.loopPotential: If Opa trusts the clock, he'll sleep through day; if he ignores it, he wakes on time but distrusts all clocks.
raw.providerRationale: Clock's directional time reversal directly prevents scheduled waking; the impossible rule is visually obvious with backward hands.
